result.title: Adaptive Skill Granularity for Coding Agents: Runtime Routing and Macro-to-Micro Recovery
result.summary: Reusable skills allow large language model agents to package task-specific procedures, tool affordances, and execution guidance into modular units. Prior work has largely studied how agents retrieve, compose, or synthesize skills before execution. In coding agents, however, execution poses an additional runtime control problem: the same task may be solved through primitive tool calls, macro skills, or hybrid execution that starts with a macro and falls back to micro-level recovery. We introduce Adaptive Skill Granularity, a framework that treats skill granularity as an action-abstraction policy conditioned on task structure, execution state, and macro-skill failures. The system combines a feature-based granularity controller and a finite-state recovery executor. We evaluate the framework with a deterministic coding-agent protocol using verifier-defined success, total cost, and process metrics such as macro adoption, failure recovery, route match, and transition correctness. Results show that fixed macro execution is efficient when applicable but brittle under mismatch, while runtime routing and explicit macro-to-micro recovery improve robustness and recover controlled macro failures that fixed-granularity execution leaves unresolved. Our findings suggest that skill libraries for coding agents should be treated not only as retrievable resources, but also as controllable, verifiable, and recoverable execution abstractions.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Adaptive Skill Granularity 框架，把代码 agent 的技能粒度当作依赖任务结构、执行状态与宏技能失败的动作抽象策略，用特征式粒度控制器加有限状态恢复执行器在运行时于宏技能和原始工具调用间路由，并以确定性协议评估成本、恢复与路由正确性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按执行状态选择抽象层级、宏失败后回退到微步骤」的控制器与恢复状态机，可能可供核查如何组织 THINK/LOOK/STOP 之间的切换与失败回退；但该工作无视觉输入与 latent 状态，仅属较远的方法线索。
